reviews.title: so fun
reviews.text:
update: sound now saves! Sound sensitive folks beware— the new version starts at 100% volume every time. There’s no way to permanently adjust or disable sound. 

 I started playing this in 2014 when it was new and was fascinated by the simple set up and rich storytelling. Once every few years I’ll come back to it. It’s fun to play with different goals in mind - how quickly, with or without huts, cover the whole map or just get what you need, etc. The new interface roll out for the 10th anniversary is overall a big improvement. As with any UI change if you’re used to the old way, it takes a while to get used to the new way. For me, the hardest thing to get used to was the fact that some of the timing and features are actually different. So some strategies I used before don’t really apply in the same way. That does add to the fun to have new challenges though. I would give this five stars

reviews.title: This Simple Task Brings Comfort
reviews.text:
I’ve had ADR since it first released and I’ve played The Ensign and A Noble Circle too. Many many many times. At this point, I’ve completed the game so many times and I’m so used to it that I can beat it in about an hour start to finish. Somehow, even…what? A decade later? I still enjoy playing the game even though I know precisely what will happen. It has become my bed time mantra. Somehow, playing this game, stoking the fire, running through the motions, has given me a way to quiet my mind and go to sleep. I literally play it every night before bed. The small lines of dialogue have become even more relatable and this game now truly brings me a sense of solace. 

When I first started, I had a sense of wonder and horror and imagination strike through me when I played the game. It’s a brilliantly done story. Done perfectly with so little. I have loved it from the start and hope to have it

reviews.text:
To be honest I had no idea what the game was before purchasing it. I read on a list somewhere that it was a good game and decided to give it a shot. It was out of my normal scope of games but after playing for a period of time I really got into the progression of everything. 

After quite a bit of progression, things just kinda stopped. I wasn’t sure how to make the next step happen or what to do. Point being, give the game a shot. It is different than most you will see but it turns out to be a lot of fun. After finishing, I actually was disappointed it was over. reviews.text: I bought this game a while ago and I finally decided to pick it up. I stoked the fire and wondered, what is here for me? I soon found out through a satisfying drip of information that there was more to this world than meets the eye. Secrets revealed, new shocking dialogue said, and a need to discover more pulled me through the game. I literally gasped at a certain part of the story (for those of you who have played it, you know EXACTLY the line). I was crushed at times but I pushed through to get to the end, and what’s this? Thank you to the wonderful devs who brought this game to life. It is an experience that I will never forget.

reviews.title: Like an existential dream
reviews.text: I’ve been playing this game since the beginning. I played on a little iPhone 4 and I was immediately hooked. I had no clue what I was doing, but I had to follow the path laid out for me. The unknowing is absolutely part of the excitement and intrigue. I can’t explain why the dark room makes me feel nostalgic, but I also feel heroic, anxious, and stupid at times. I’ve played several times in different ways, which is part of the adventure. I’ve read many of the critiques, including one that called the good reviews a conSpiracy! This made me laugh. I can understand how a ppl so accustom to extremely colorful graphics and forceful game play may feel uncomfortable, confused, and even bored with a game that requires reading and thinking. If you want an experience in gaming, one that requires your mind and heart in some way, get this game.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text:
Took me 182 minutes to finish the game and it was fantastic, I found myself drawn in and not wanting to put it down. It can be slow at first, and making a functioning economy can be difficult but it’s all about the challenge. Every time I died on the dusty path made me a little upset but I just wanted revenge and to see what was farther out. Game can feel grindy at some times but picks right back up after a little bit. Going to play through again with different styles. Worth the 2$ for sure. If you have trouble justifying the price, think about it as a three hour movie for 2$, that you control, that you can play over and over again, and that you own forever. It’s a good investment I think. I might try to play the web version. 

Overall, great game and good developers. Worth the 2$ and has replay value. Good game 5 stars

reviews.title: Something Worth Experiencing
reviews.text: A Dark Room is one of my most recommended apps when someone asks me for a game on the App Store to play. It starts as a simple resource management game but builds into something much more than expected. I can't wait to see what else Michael and Amir have in store. Thank you to them for making such a worthwhile experience. The ending is truly something special. I purchased The Ensign minutes after completing this. If there is any game worth playing on the App Store right now, it's this. From the moment you press light fire to your thousandth death on the dusty trail during your hundredth play through makes it all worth it for the second you see your starship fly into the unknown the game holds puts you on the edge of seat. To reiterate I cannot recommend this game to people enough.

reviews.title: Brilliant Game
reviews.text: I highly recommend this game to anyone with an active imagination or anyone who loves falling into a story. This game places you in the middle of mind-bending twists and forces fate upon you in a way that leaves you wondering what could have been. The writers and creators of this game have done an incredible job building a world that reveals itself the more you play, build and explore. I wish I could review every aspect of this game, but there are so many twists that I would not want to spoil the surprises for anyone! After becoming invested in the story and completing the game the first time, it is so fun to go back and figure out how you could have pushed the limits even further. I greatly enjoyed this game and have purchased the prequel to enjoy as well. Super high recommendation for this game and anything this developer comes out with! Download this game!

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text:
I played this game a few years ago, on the old version which is funnily enough, no longer available in the states. Even after all of this time, I am still just as in love with this game as I was when I first started. The storyline is very interesting and the subtle shift from villagers to the enslaved adds even another level a story depth which I just adore. Overall I love this game, but if one thing were to be improved, I would love if there was more locations or different enemies, since after a few cities, you know exactly the order and difficulty of the foes. But, besides that, I don’t really have any complaints. If you’re looking for an addicting game with a subtle, yet mesmerizing plot, this is for you~

Thank you Michael and Amir for making such a beautiful game, you really did an amazing job.

reviews.title: A Simple but Enthralling Experience
reviews.text: A Dark Room is a game that takes a simple premise, and finds a way to make it interesting and engaging. There's no need for any highly developed visuals or cinematic sequences - the limited amount of information the game gives you is more than enough to not only build a world worth exploring and understanding, but to keep you invested until the end. The game may not be for everyone, as it lacks a lot of the superficial details that many modern games focus on, and this may be a characteristic that can be hard for some to engage with. But if you can compensate for the lack of superficial detail with you own imagination and curiosity(we do that with books all the time), this game will provide a truly unique and memorable experience, and is well worth the price point.

reviews.title: 10/10 would recommend
reviews.text: This game is a beautifully written story with phenomenal structure. It seems to start out slow, but is only the beginning of an eerie story that can be anything you imagine it to be. I’ve bought this game, thoroughly enjoyed it and redownloaded it years later to enjoy it again. But as the maker of the game states, you can really only experience your first experience once. My first experience will always be the best. Another respectable aspect to this game is the physical format of its layout. An easy to follow screen with understandable tabs makes the game comfortable to run and leaves out anything that could possibly form an image for you. The game is literally what you make it. Give it a chance. ~May the fire burn brightly for you, may it keep you warm~

reviews.title: Still the best app on the App Store
reviews.text: Recently I redownloaded this app not having played it for about 3 years.  I remembered the general idea of the game and the end result, but I forgot a lot of the major sequence events throughout. Just like the first time I played it, I had a surreal experience. This game is unlike anything you will see. It does what a lot of games fail to do- it does not only provide entertainment, but it interacts with your life outside of the game; it makes you feel something very profound that works its way into your thoughts outside the virtual world. I have thought about its message countless times and it amazes me to this day how such a simply designed text based game was able to have such an impact. Worth every penny.

reviews.title: Absolutely worth completing.
reviews.text: When you begin playing A Dark Room, it seems on the surface to simply be a text-based survival and accumulation game. It is a slow start, extremely minimalist and not immediately rewarding, which will turn most app game players off. As you keep playing through, it becomes clear that it is so much more than a survival game - it contains a powerful story that is intimately affecting and confronts the player’s preconceptions of accumulation and progress as being inherently good. The gameplay is frustrating, almost claustrophobic at times, and the plot is bleak and disturbing. Beyond this, though, the game contains its own sort of haunting beauty that stays with you long after completion. The secrets at the end of the game are worth sticking it out for!

reviews.title: No sound- BUT still an awesome game
reviews.text:
I was obsessed with the browser version of the game so I had to get the app, but there’s no sound! The sound was my favorite part of the game. I was promised sound and that’s nonexistent. So disappointing I feel like the excitement has been ruined.
—
That was my initial feedback, but I was too curious to obtain the lore so I played anyway. I miss the spooky atmosphere of the desktop version HOWEVER I LOVE this game!! The lore is incredible and I love how each different dialogue and ending challenged my preconceived idea of the world. It was so fun to put the puzzle pieces together. So yeah, I miss the infrastructure and sound of the desktop version, but I stayed for the storyline and I’m so glad I did.

reviews.title: Great game!
reviews.text:
The only reason I gave this game 4 instead of 5 stars was due to the lack of any visual/audible stimulation outside of words, symbols, and lettering, which I know was the point of the game, but I personally, would have gotten much more satisfaction with some brief, but additional sounds and visuals.

 With that said, the developers did an outstanding job creating this world using the simplest of artistic concepts to drive home the ultimate vision and goal they had in mind for this game- to stimulate the mind and create an in-depth world for the player to visualize through words and simplicity- and they did so very effectively and beautifully. 

Overall, very addictive despite the lack of visuals or sounds. It was an OCDer’s HEAVEN when venturing out to reveal every last inch of the map. Kept you on your toes and guessing over and over. Bravo!

reviews.title: Minimalist wording andlayout
reviews.text: First the good, the game is fully accessible with voiceover. It turns out the developer took special effort to learn about that and do it. Also, ad free. It also doesn’t have in app purchases that basically make you feel like you’re wasting effort if you can’t afford to pay a lot, which makes it stand out from the other games because they like to nickel and dime you to death. the minimalist interface is a good thing. The minimalist wording is not because I am a grammar nerd and like complete sentences, more options and clear plots.. I also don’t particularly like the plot after my first Playthrough and I have to enjoy the plot to wanna play again. Therefore, it only gets a four-star, even though it probably does deserve a five.

reviews.title: I love it. But
reviews.text: I played this game for two weeks and completed it. Very fun to play and I love it. I only have one small complaint. The fact that each time you die on the dusty path you lose everything that you gathered. There were many times where I would gather so many important things and new ones to that I forgotten where I found them and I would die and lose all of it. This makes the game boring and frustrating to . I don’t know if the sequel of this game is like this to, but if it is, I am not buying it until this issue has been fixed. I consider this an issue not a challenge. Thank you very much for your understanding and I hope you read this review developer. And thank you once again for this great game

reviews.title: Wonderfully unique
reviews.text: Truly a unique game. One of a kind. I love this approach to a game, it is very simplistic yet fascinating. I’ve never seen anything like it before and never experienced anything like it before. The only thing I would say could be better is adding sound effects (even just button sounds) but the quietness also does liberties to the unsettling feeling throughout. Playing your own music playlist in the background is fun too. I think everyone should try this out, it’s so fun to figure out the mechanics as you go on, and the story, though vague is so interesting. I hope to get the prequel game and I hope to see more games from the developer one day!

reviews.title: disappointed with no options for villager freedom
reviews.text: Did a run without building any structures that would enslave the villagers. No clearing mines, no building lodge, nothing. Even tried not to kill people in other cities. Got extremely far then stalled because no enemies drop sulfur and you need sulphur to eventually lift off by building the armory. The sulfur mine immediately enslaved my villagers and the builder got mad at me. There's no way to give the villagers a home without eventually hurting them and that makes me sad - clearly they need some help, they're always struggling when they arrive. Still an awesome game and I enjoy the continuous exploration. Please let me be nice to these people though. Thanks

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text: I played this game once on the web a couple of years ago and purchased the iOS version, but I never opened the app or finished the web version. Today, while looking through my purchase history, I saw ADR and was immediately thrown back to the intrigue I felt when playing the web version and proceeded to download it. I was sucked into the story again and even restarted a couple of times when I realized there were perks that assist in exploring the world in the hopes of getting them earlier. While it is a simplistic game, there is an in-depth story that leaves you kind of unsettled but definitely needing to know more. I only wish I could play it for the first time again.

reviews.title: A letter to the Creators
reviews.text:
I have loved this game my whole life. I played it when I was younger for the first time, and listened to all the audio after I completed it. It meant so much to me to hear that audio, and this game will forever hold a place in my heart.

This game gave kid me a different perspective on the world, while also giving me hours of entertainment. I think in total I’ve completed the game 4 or 5 times. 

Now that I’m an adult, I’m currently in college, I don’t have time to play it all the way through anymore. I hope everyone gets this game, and considers donating. The creators put their heart and soul into this game, and I will forever love them for it.

reviews.title: One of my fav repeat games!
reviews.text:
I’ve been playing this game on and off for several years now, and this is the first time I played it on mobile. And I only started playing it on mobile, because I saw that you guys had a prequel called The Ensign.

For other players:

reviews.title: There are no words
reviews.text:
There are no real words to describe how you will feel after you complete this game. Your experience is your own, but I had chills for a while. I became so attached to this world, and I greatly appreciate the graphics. From what you catch and understand to what dialogue goes right over your head. Your experience is your own. I played through this game once several years ago and didn’t think much of it. I played through it again and I’m speechless. There’s so much I missed and so much more I understand through the beautifully done dialogue once you complete the game.

Keep wandering Wanderer m

reviews.title: New Layout Blues
reviews.text: Was my favorite. Could play it for hours. New layout has cart wood and check traps buttons annoyingly close and shoved in corner. Seemingly they wanted to expand middle area info. I don’t know how it could be possible, but these layout changes have shifted this from a game I would play back to back to back— to a game I can’t force myself to get through one time. Seriously, I go back to it and think maybe I just haven’t given it a chance. But having the buttons you most need to tap so close and or so high up, makes it feel like a tedious clerical task instead of an intuitive journey. And I love this game. Want to contact programers and ask them to please change it back to the original. I’ve uninstalled and reinstalled with hope that they might have changed it back, but no luck.  Dear Programmers: the past layout was perfect. Your game was brilliant. Please restore it. Thank you.

reviews.title: Very Thankful
reviews.text: I bought this game when I was about 16-17… 28 now. It’s always just been in my library and I would play it from time to time but never put in real effort. Going through some difficult times at the moment, I remembered this game and downloaded it again and beat it. Not sure how to explain it, but it felt like home every time I sat down to play it. A dark story, but very comfy, great audio/sounds.. this game is just great. I wish there was a pt 2, or another game similar to this one. Thank you so much for making this game. I’m doing another playthrough right now. This game has been here for me when real people weren’t.

reviews.title: Beautiful, immersive game.
reviews.text:
For years, I’ve started and then forgotten about A Dark Room, but I always really enjoyed playing it. This time, I committed to finishing, and I’m so glad I did. Finally getting to experience the complete narrative was so rewarding and chilling. The secrets from the devs made finishing even more fun.

Despite its minimalistic interface, ADR is surprisingly visual. Very quickly, I was able to see the village, the builder, the gaunt man, the mines, the dusty path and everything the game had to offer in my head. It added a level of immersion that I don’t often get in iOS games.

Overall, I’m so glad I finally finished this game. Can’t wait to try it out without building huts!

reviews.title: My first textie—addictive
reviews.text: I came to computer gaming later than many—my first was the “Myst” series, and when I found this one recently on the app store, I questioned why it was available. For the first 15 minutes I played it, I found it absurdly simplistic and uninteresting (with the display capabilities of my iPad, why am I staring at naked text??). I set it aside for weeks, then retried it, and finally ended up enraptured. Trying to figure out the most productive ratio of work allocation, gambling on improving my odds by loading up on valuables while not taking more than I was willing to risk losing, and trying to interpret the builder’s sorrowful commentary were really engaging and intriguing.

reviews.title: Not a gamer but totally hooked.
reviews.text:
I've never been into games, but saw a review on HuffPost and thought I'd try it on a lark. I was hooked. I've never been addicted to a game before and I spent three days addicted- I slept less and avoided other things if I could. I liked it never told you what to do- you had to just figure it out. Towards the end it moved slower- didn't find/earn new things, so my interest lagged some. I plan to play it again now that I "get it".  Now I must do all the housework I've neglected...

Update 2018: have played several more times in past years, for the challenge, the uniqueness, and just overall what it says about us and society

reviews.title: Wowwww what a journey.
reviews.text: I just recently moved my life across the country and it’s been alright. every night I sit outside look at the stars and listen to the wind. Always thinking about the past I remember playing a game where I lit a fire embarked on journeys and finding alien artifacts, never knowing what to do with them. I scrambled for a week trying to find the game I played 8 years ago and here I am. At last I can say I finally found it, beat it and getting a piece of mind. I’m writing this listening the wind again wondering where my next journey begins. What an amazing game thank you for the experience again.

reviews.title: Still go back to it every so often
reviews.text: I remember playing the browser version of this game several years ago, and being intrigued by finding it in the App Store. It might seem strange to pay for a game you’d played through for free but for the price, why not? The mobile game is a sufficient upgrade and worth the price a few times over. The simple, unique experience is something I find myself going back and reliving every so often. If you’ve never tried the game before and happen upon this, give it a shot, just try to be patient in the opening sequence.

reviews.title: Captivating and Addictive
reviews.text: I came across the web version of this game randomly after searching for fun games to play while bored online. After a short session, I was hooked. Realizing there was an IOS version of the game, I got it immediately. This is the perfect time passing game that keeps you enthralled and entertained the entire 3-4 hour journey. The game is both rewarding and punishing at times but never trades your enjoyment for frustration. The game begins like a resource clicker-type-game, and then expands into a mystery adventure. This game is for someone who loves indie developed games and simplistic designs. Excited to play the prequel!

reviews.title: Fantastic Game
reviews.text: I tested out this game a long time ago, played for a few hours, and didn’t really get into it beyond a piqued interest. I tried it again this weekend, and WHAT. A. RIDE. I had no idea what this game was capable of being, especially as you go further along. The game flawlessly teaches you how it should be played without a tutorial, or any direct indication of what you should do next. The story is told beautifully without the mention of any names, just small changes to details that you only notice after skipping past them the first time they came up. 5/5, would absolutely recommend to all my friends. Great job!!

reviews.title: Such An Intriguing Game
reviews.text: At first, I was pretty skeptical of the game. Reading a couple reviews is what really pushed me to buy ADR. When I started playing, I admit was confused and was starting to doubt the game. But I’m not a person to give up too easily. So I continued with the game, the more I play the more I felt curious and engulfed by ADR. There are feelings that this game will make you feel that other games will not. It’s such a simple game but it can also make you feel such complex feelings. I definitely recommend this game to everyone, just give it a chance. I promise ADR will give you a new experience. May the fire burn brightly for you, make it keep you warm.

reviews.title: Loved it! However,
reviews.text: I was super enjoying the game, and had finally figured out how to play it. then I accidentally hit the button to take the action that ends the game, and there was no undo. I know this game is like old enough to be in middle school at this point, but i’d really have appreciated a confirmation screen there, and it would have been appropriate to the story to have it there. After ~550 minutes of play, just because of fat fingering, I ended the story on less than ideal circumstances. I also just was not ready to say goodbye to it 😭 beautiful game but I am taking off a star for that. Highly recommended however!

reviews.title: Wonder and exploration await
reviews.text:
I distinctly remember my first play through, my 7th grade self found a dark room on a school computer and it slowly began to occupy my mind during the lulls in Texas history. The slow creep of new mechanics and mysteries about the unique world you’re dropped into practically beg you to explore the dusty path and the subtle lore hidden throughout all aspects of the game. The minimalistic nature of the game encourages you to fill in the lore of the world yourself, allowing each player’s journey to be their own, as well as providing very satisfying revelations when you stumble upon some knew knowledge. 
 May the fire burn bright for you, may it keep you warm.

reviews.title: Proof that a game doesn’t need stunning graphics to be amazing
reviews.text:
Overall this game is amazing, a simple story full of mystery and intrigue. The curve of new things to do is perfectly laid out allowing for the best feeling of satisfaction. I have replayed this game many times over the years, and it still holds up

Only reason for 4/5 stars is that the new loot screen is very hard to manage, it is hard to tell what you have and what you don’t, the previous layout was flawless and I would strongly recommend resetting it to something like that as trying to figure out if I have each item on my body takes 4x as long now

reviews.title: Love this game! Grabs you
reviews.text:
If you’re tired of flashy, dopamine-addiction-fueling, cookie-cutter, thoughtless push button games they’ve been churning out, this game is for you.
It grabs you and rewards you for curiosity and takes you to the stars and gives you a ride for your life. I downloaded it years ago and I’m still playing it. It has a beautifully, crafted simplicity, challenges you on multiple mechanics I’ve never encounters before. 

You’ll never see ending coming. Or beginning. Or the middle. Great if you got plane rides or long waits. Saves your progress and tells you a great story.

reviews.title: Wow.
reviews.text: I’ve played this game before, a long time ago. I beat it once but didn’t take time to enjoy the ending. Today after about 3.5 hours of casual gameplay over 3 days I beat it for the 2nd time. Taking time to listen to the developers words is great. Incredible game. Looking forward to starting the ensign. I’ve been looking forward to this for a long time. Thank you for this experience. Some people will never know the time & work that goes into creating such an addictive game in this format. I sure won’t. But I  appreciate it. GG , let’s see where the ensign takes us

reviews.title: Very Impressive, Great Game
reviews.text: I played this game for the first time a couple years back and loved it, just re-downloaded a couple days ago and already went through it twice.  Really interesting concept and the program is awesome, the fact that one dude developed the whole app is super dope. I would recommend this to anyone that appreciates relatively simplistic (in terms of the layout) but engaging games.  It’s not flashy and the visuals don’t stun you, but that’s honestly part of what makes the game so great, how plain he/she left the program with almost no graphics. I would rate this 6 stars if I could, easily one of my favorite games.

reviews.title: Still enjoyable after all these years
reviews.text: I picked this game up several years ago and probably play it again once every year and a half or so. As the developer points out, you can really only experience this game for the first time once. But long enough gaps in replay seems to recapture enough of the magic for me. The game is quite unconventional and rewards those with enough patience to feel it out and explore. The audio logs after beating it once are interesting, but seem to be bugged now - The game crashes after each log completes and you have to restart to hear the next one.

reviews.title: Unlike anything I’ve played before.
reviews.text:
Although I agree with most of the reviews, I’m not going to gush over this game and make you think it’s Gods gift to text based games, as this is my first, but I will say as a culminate experience, it is without a doubt worth your money and 5 stars. My only complaint would be I wish it had its own soundtrack. Just a subtle breeze blowing through the trees while you’re managing your village. Music, or even ambient sounds, I’ve found, profoundly impact video games, especially ones as meaningful as ADR. 

Outside of that, as my first text based game, it was enjoyable and I feel like I’ve been missing out on a very special genre of video games. At 35 years, I’ve missed a lot of good games over the years and thankfully ADR has opened my eyes.

Honestly, after beating the game, the extra stuff in the menu from these guys would have provoked me to give 5 stars even if the game was abysmal. It w

reviews.title: Better than I could have imagined
reviews.text: Finished in 144 minutes, and I wish it took longer. Played straight through with out putting my phone down once. It’s the best way to play this game. I was completely immersed in a text based game, emotionally attached to the characters and the world in my mind. The simplicity of the story line leaves a lot to the imagination, but in a good way. I was shocked at the twists that come along the way, and how addicting it became. The developers are geniuses. You truly can only experience the game for the first time, once, and it’s brilliant. May the fire burn brightly for you, may it keep you warm.

reviews.title: Absolutely Glorious
reviews.text: I didn’t really know what to expect from this game when i first purchased it, but I’m so glad I did. The simplicity of this app makes it so complex, and it left me confused and wondering, but the storyline was so odd i couldn’t stop progressing. I feel that the simplest of games are always the best. The effort and detail was extraordinary. It was definitely worth the money I spent on it. I highly recommend this game, and it never gets old the more you play it. If you start again, there’s always something you find that you never saw before. I absolutely love this game, and I feel I always will.

reviews.title: Simple yet not in the best ways.
reviews.text: This game is fantastic. If you've never played it before the 1$ price is trivial compared to what you'll get from this game. The story and gameplay is very well crafted in its own unique ways. I've had this game for a long time now and have played it a handful of times. Stuck at the airport or some other place? This is perfect for those situations. No need to be staring at the screen unless you can perfectly time hitting a pause button. If it even exists in other games. Bottom line is. Get this game. Enjoy it to its fullest and then some. And let everyone else know about it.

reviews.title: Simple But Stunning
reviews.text:
I love text based adventure games so when I found this I thought I’d give it a whirl. Here I am after binging on the game continuously for about 2 and 1/2 hours straight. The ending just left me wanting more, and I guarantee you if you enjoy text based games where you picture the story and the action playing out in your head, then this is simply a must for you. No ads, no glitches (that I found in my play-through), no micro transactions, it’s a gem of a game. My only critique is a lack of ambient music, but I just played my own in the background, otherwise a perfect game. 

5 Stars ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️

reviews.title: A truly satisfying experience
reviews.text:
Got the new iPhone yesterday. So wanted to play some new games to enjoy the bigger screen. Came across this text based adventure and couldn’t resist. It had been a while since I last played a text based game and decided to give this a shot. Needless to say, I wasn’t disappointed. 
The game is simple to begin and has an amazing progression. This can be a case in study for tutorial done right, without making it seem like a tutorial. 
What this game lacks in visuals, it more than makes up for it with its soul. A truly amazing experience. 
Can’t wait to start a new adventure.

reviews.title: Best Game Ever!!!! Seriously!
reviews.text:
This is hands down the best game I’ve ever played. I’ve gone through it multiple times now, and every single playthrough feels just as exciting and fresh as the first. The story is gripping, the gameplay is smooth and addictive, and the little details make it clear how much care went into crafting this adventure! 

It’s rare to find a game that sticks with you like this, but this one has truly set the standard. Over the years, I keep downloading this game and playing! If I could give it more than 5 stars, I would! Simple and Perfect!

reviews.title: Incredible story, unique gameplay like nothing else
reviews.text: I love this app. I have beat it at least 5 times, probably more. What I love is the story. It's not your typical click dialogue and interact story, yet it has that feel. Your trying to survive in this world, and yet this story progresses around you. It's incredible. The freedom of the player yet the solid storyline are beautiful when viewed through the minimalist game play. There are no flashy decals, or crazy graphics, because that's not the point. It's the story, and allowing the user to have the freedom to choose while demonstrating their theme. Beautiful, gaming and storytelling.

reviews.title: Wonderful experience
reviews.text: I remember downloading this game as a young teen. Throughout the years since then I found myself randomly thinking of playing. I’ve played several times before and have beat this game twice. Both times I’ve played through have been amazing. The emotions I feel for characters I can’t even see blows my mind. This game is so different than anything else I’ve played yet it strikes some cord in my body that gets me through every play through. I’m very excited to play the next one for the first time!

reviews.title: Awesome start to finish
reviews.text: Started ADR a few years ago when I was in highschool workin on an island in the middle of a lake with no cell reception. Now almost a decade later I saw it again and remembered how much cool it was back then. Started it while on a flight cross country and finished the game a few days later (Today). It is just as good as I remembered, and then some, especially since I actually completed it this time around. Definitely recommend 100%, this is the first review I've ever written, but it deserves it. No if you'll excuse me, I need to see what's goin on with these huts...

reviews.title: No game can impact you like this one
reviews.text: After only my second complete play through a couple years later I am still amazed at how addicting this game is. Not only does it feed my addiction through progression, but through the hunger for me power and adventure.  The actions I must commit truly question my moral character, who I am and what I’m doing in this wonderfully built universe. It truly was an incredible experience like nothing else on mobile. I am compelled to play the ensign again, listen to all the post game content and once again, thirst for me.  Thank you for this incredible experience.

reviews.title: Stoke fire - the line is back!
reviews.text:
Thank you for the recent font and UI updates. This feels more like the original. I hated that other font, this new one is much easier on the eyes. Will the app icon get an update as well? 

First play through was back in 2014. I picked this back up a week or two ago and had to stop playing cause it was unrecognizable to me. Lack of the stoke line shook me. It is so iconic!!! 

The line is back with the update as well as some needed improvements - thanks for listening to the feedback from other “original UI” players.🫡

reviews.title: Masterpiece
reviews.text: This game was hands down the best game I have ever played on my phone. It was creative, unique, challenging, simple controls  but very complex story and meaning behind every text that you read or choice you get. No other game in the App Store has given me a sense of urgency or joy. No other game has given me the feeling of danger and loss. I would actually be scared to venture out and explore because I might loose my stuff or I might stumble on a sniper. Every step I took off that road I could feel my heart rate go up. I can't wait to play the pre-sequel. This game was brilliant keep up the good work.

reviews.title: Hard Mode Please!
reviews.text:
Edit: I miss the old version! The one where you start off with nothing! If you could just make it so I could turn off getting those extra supplies at the start, I would be very grateful

This is an amazing game. I go to it whenever I need something familiar and comforting, and it never lets me down. Amir has created a terrific world and combined it with a beautiful gameplay and an excellent story. It can be dark at times, but it's always worth a play through. I have his other two games as well and they're also fantastic. They're well worth it.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: This game is really, and I mean, really good. It took me awhile to finish (small attention spans and lots of wandering), but the pacing was excellent. It is a game that provides the flexibility to either speed through or it really just mess around and enjoy it. It has a lot of mysterious and foreboding elements to it, but really excels at providing a gratifying way to track your progress. It is cynical, yet hopeful. It was worth every bit of the $1.99 without any ads or in-game purchases. Will definitely be buying other games from the devs. Great job, guys. Keep it up and don’t change a thing.

reviews.title: Simple, Elegant Game Design
reviews.text:
A Dark Room hooks you immediately with its mysterious and minimalist take on an action-adventure/management sim. It takes a novelistic approach to providing you with only the information you need to advance the game and narrative elements, trusting your imagination to fill in the rest, while managing to deliver a palpable experience that’ll have you chasing down answers and questioning what you’re willing to do to get them.

Don’t skip A Dark Room. It’s one of the most original mobile games you’ll have the privilege of playing.

reviews.title: An amazing game
reviews.text: I’ve played through this game at least a dozen times, probably more. Its hard to put into words what this game means to me. I love it’s minimal interface and the richness of the gameplay. It is well thought out and intuitive in how it unrolls features as the user continues on their journey. Playing with huts or without is equally fun and entertaining. This game is a benchmark and a standard with which most other games pale in comparison. Good games entertain once. Great games continue to entertain after the first play through. This is a great game.

reviews.title: One of my favorite games of all time
reviews.text:
I just replayed this after a few years and wanted to hop on to show my appreciation because this is still one of the best out there! The way the story builds mystery and slowly unfolds in unexpected ways is genius. The gameplay is simple but challenging, and is just frustrating enough to make you want to beat it without sucking out the fun. 

There’s also a prequel game called the ensign, which is equally brilliant (if not more so). If you’re considering getting this game, do it!! It’s truly one of a kind.

reviews.title: Waste an evening in someone else’s moral experiment
reviews.text:
A Dark Room is less a game and more a blunt philosophical experiment. It hides its mechanics, offers almost no fine-grained control, and forces players into major moral consequences through opaque, all-or-nothing systems.

What frustrated me most is that it gives you almost no ability to practice nuance. You can’t reassign labor, reprioritize systems, or gently tune anything. When something goes wrong, it doesn’t teach you… it just escalates, often with heavy moral weight. It feels like being trapped inside someone else’s thought experiment rather than being invited to build your own.

I don’t mind difficult themes. I mind when a game removes agency and then lectures me about the lack of it. I wanted to build something humane, but the game doesn’t really let you do that with intention, it only lets you discover, through blunt force, what happens when systems go bad.

That may be powerful

reviews.title: Captivating and Intriguing
reviews.text:
One of the simplest games I have played, but also the most emotionally rewarding. With beautiful and dark twists and narrative throughout I was always interested in going further. At first I felt disappointment when the fire was lit, the dark room wasn’t dark anymore. The most agonizing 15 seconds of gameplay was waiting for that next bit of narrative, and the most rewarding when finding out the fire wasn’t the only important thing to take care of…

May the fire burn brightly for you. May it keep you warm.

reviews.title: Engaging Imaginary Imagery
reviews.text:
Read somewhere it was a top app.  Thought I’d give it a go....  

In the early 80’s, text adventure games were the precursors of modern, computer based, video games.  Immediately, this reminded me of those early games - completely cerebral.  Eventually, the game gives way to the current fad of rapid tapping to win battles, but all the while you’re gaining knowledge and playing with strategy. (So, this felt acceptable.)

I was surprised at it’s subtle draw.  I found myself wanting to play it, late at night, to wind down.  At points I felt compelled to conquer the game, but could easily put it down.  Starting up again was always easy.  I welcomed that attribute more than I realized at first.  The pacing is just right. (Good job, guys.)

It’s a neat game and a nice change of pace from the typical, graphic intensive, games I usually play.  I will likely seek more colorful renditions, of conc

reviews.title: What an experience
reviews.text: I remember as a small kid back in 9th grade when this game was released. It was a part of a free app of the week deal, and I loved checking out those games. This mobile game, unlike others, had a story to tell. As I grew older and can understand more than I used to in this game, I loved the tension that was released throughout this game and I am glad I revisited this masterpiece 4 years later. I can not wait to try out the prequel and the newer game that you have created. Again, 5 years from your amazing creation, job well done my good sir. Job well done.

reviews.title: More fun than you’d expect
reviews.text: 173 minutes to beat it here... very fun game.. I was hoping for more of a difficult task in building up the thing at the end (don't want to spoil). I had heard that a certain item was important, so I held onto it every time I saw it.  I kinda wish you needed a few different materials to rebuild it... but I don't think that takes away anything from how great the game is.. this is more of an afterthought just so I could have an excuse to keep playing the game for longer than it took me.

reviews.title: Most amazing game ever
reviews.text: This game has to be one of the the greatest games ever capturing the incredible survival experience... in words, yes this game is entirely words but don’t be discouraged it is not a reading type of game pictures are just replaced with words and really like the look and feel of it it gives a nice and clean looking game with awesome adventure and resource management. And overall this game is definitely worth the money but to be honest the second one isn’t good just play the first one plz devs make a third one like this game id buy it like many others.

reviews.title: A true gaming experience
reviews.text:
This is the one app on my phone that I can truly say I enjoy playing to the fullest extent. It is original, it is true to itself, and offers all of its content for its purchase price. 

The story is eerie, disturbing, and told in a powerfully simple way. Each line of story leaves you aching for the next one and initiates a drive to find the next objective. 

I've never had so much fun staring at a screen full of text. Don't let the lack of graphics prematurely chase you away. The interface is charming and drives the mystery home.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text:
This game is beautiful, it tells a tragic, somber, yet inspirational and introspective story in such a simple way. From the moment you begin the game you will notice that it is not akin to any other gaming experience. Many, will at this point give in and review bomb the app. However, give this game a shot and I guarantee that you will enjoy yourself. This game stands either as a resource management, explorative, or social commentary game. In the end, A Dark Room is what you make of it. I hope you enjoy it as much as I have.

May the fire burn brightly for you, may it keep you warm.

reviews.title: An obscure game more should know
reviews.text:
A Dark Room is a game with depth you don’t find in every game. It’s simple, with no visuals and only text to guide you, but it still manages to tell a vivid story. How you interpret that story is up to you. Is it about survival? Love? Greed? The game is whatever you want it to be, and it can be as long or short as you want it to be. It’s all up to you. 
     The devs have made a truly clever game I’m sad I’ve finished. I thoroughly enjoyed every moment, thank you for making such an awesome and memorable game. :)

reviews.title: Really loved this
reviews.text: This is a unique experience more than a game for me. I really enjoyed experiencing it, I didn’t always enjoy playing it. I had never played an idle game before and had a really hard time learning how the game worked but eventually I noticed and googled things that really made the game more fun. Understanding traversing the map and what each letter meant and that the compass was helping lead me through the game in a linear progression helped.  Also learning that dying can actually be good also helped.

reviews.title: Awesome game
reviews.text: I first downloaded this game when it came out and never really understood it at the time and had downloaded it because it was at the top of the charts. Weird reason I know. But, as I got more into text based rpgs and what not I found myself brought back to a dark room when someone recommended it to me. Such a dark and fantastically written story at the same time while remaining simplistic. I’ve played through it so many times now. Still haven’t beaten it without huts lol. But I love this game and maybe I should try the prequel.

reviews.title: The best
reviews.text: This is hands down my favorite game of all time. If I would have paid 60 dollars for the experience I have experienced and I have donated btw. When I said this was a game I lied, this is an experience. It is so immersive despite the simple design. If you do decide to purchase this (do) make sure you listen to all of the audio clips at the end. It just shows you how much time the developers put into the game. Did you know you could play this blind!?!? Crazy. It is so worth your money like no joke just give it a chance

reviews.title: Such a great game! Give it a try!
reviews.text: Like many people, I was skeptical, I played and I quit, erased it about 2-3 years ago, remembered how great of a game it was while going through my downloaded apps. So I downloaded it again yesterday, I don’t know why I ever quit playing it. This has to be the most simple but detailed game. You don’t have much to go based off of but it’s enough for you to visualize, almost like reading a book. It’s a great game completely worth the money. The best part is when you beat it and find the hidden stuff!

reviews.title: Wow!!
reviews.text: I have been playing games my entire life. I love video games and everything they bring to the table. “A Dark Room” is one of the best games I have ever played, not just mobile games, ALL GAMES! I love the lack of knowledge you have in the beginning and how a certain path to follow is not given. You decide how this story ends. How the developers foster a level of curiosity that I have never felt before is a true work of art. I would give 10 stars if I could. Absolutely wonderful game. Thank you so much. Can’t wait to play the prequel!

reviews.title: Unexpectedly poignant
reviews.text:
This game is slow burning, but really quite beautiful. It progresses seamlessly too. It takes just the right amount of time to complete.

I would definitely play this game if you’re looking for an abstract, minimal adventure game where you get to kind of interpret the story and the world yourself— and then have your preconceived notions about it shaken up as the game develops. You also get to listen to the game’s developers talk about all the secrets and stuff after, and that debriefing made everything make much more sense!

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text:
This game is a work of art the time put into making payed off immensely as this game combines storytelling a sense of mystery and adventure leaving the player intrigued but want to find out more, to find the end. I’ve never seen another game that does what this game does even close to as well as it does it, the storyline is thrilling the gameplay is surprisingly fun.
     
     Altogether this is a game I would recommend to anybody even my great grandpa who hates smart phones would love at least some part of this game if not all of it!

reviews.title: Best dollar I've ever spent.
reviews.text: I've never found an app as in depth as this. It's serene. From the first time you press the stoke fire button to the time when your journey ends (or doesn't), you are emotionally attached. There are so many things you can pick up on that aren't said directly. It isn't needed to have a team of 100 developers and millions of dollars to make a game. This, this is without a doubt the best game I've ever played. It's all you could want.

reviews.title: I loved this game, not now…
reviews.text: ADR was more than a game for me. The story was beautiful, and poetic and tragic, and (dare I say) life changing. Yes, gameplay was a grind in the middle, but it was for a purpose. The UI was easy and navigable on a phone, it did simplicity extremely well. An absolute hidden gem. The update has destroyed all of my goodwill (most likely) the goodwill of the community that’s been here from the beginning. IMHO the Dev traded all of the charm of this experience for a UI (seemingly) designed for a child on an iPad with attention issues. I would gladly pay $50 for the original game back, this disappointing monstrosity is being deleted from my devices. I see a compromise being “ADR classic” and “ADR +”. DEV—Please don’t wreck ‘The Ensign’. #notmyADR

reviews.title: Well worth the cost and time
reviews.text:
I had played the desktop version of this before but never got very far. On vacation a friend recommended the app and it was the perfect thing to kill time. The scraps of story were interesting and after playing it through once I immediately wanted to do it again. 

Four stars because I noticed that sometimes the response time would be extremely slow - it could make it very hard to move around the map and made the final section impossible the first time I tried it.

reviews.title: Quaint.  Love the developer commentaries at the end.
reviews.text:
I initially gave this game 3 stars, but after completing it, I went back once more to complete “without huts” and started listening to the developer commentaries.  I think that little bit of extra information made the game significantly more interesting, and, in a way, ..real.

Still I say, it’s worth the $2, it makes me a bit nostalgic for true text games, but now I also think, it is a great variation on the text games of yore.  Here’s hoping it can be developed into a whole new genre.

Awake.  Head throbbing.  Light the fire.

reviews.title: Incredible
reviews.text: I have never been so intellectually and weirdly enough, emotionally moved by this game. The game forces you to decipher a storyline that is vague but still keep you intrigued throughout. Playing this game makes you think deeply about the meaning of existence and what it truly takes to survive. The plot line was so precisely portrayed with merely clues and hints to guide you. This RPG allows the player to create their own image of the games world in their head. The developers are very intelligent and creative minds, I would suggest this to anyone!!!!

reviews.title: Quality game, highly worth it
reviews.text:
I never write reviews for apps but I just had to for this one!

This game is a breath of fresh air in the domain of mobile games these days. Not only is it NOT littered with ads and in-app purchases, it’s a piece of art! With genuinely interesting story elements and twists, it has a way of continually expanding your curiosity, the urge to press that “cart wood” or the “embark” button growing greater and greater. I encourage you to stare into the abyss, and see what the abyss does in return…

reviews.title: Incredible Game, must buy!
reviews.text: When I first got the game I found it really boring because of how simple it was and how it moved slowly so I didn’t play it for a while. Then a few month later I revisited it and tried playing it again. If you wait a bit the game gets better and better and the way you keep finding new things is fun! I know at the very beginning it’s boring but give it a chance, it became very addicting to me :)

reviews.title: Definitely suggest it
reviews.text: The only thing I will say without spoiling anything is that this game is unlike any other game I’ve ever played before in my life. And I’ve played a lot of games in my lifetime, but this is the most unique. When I first read some reviews I was skeptical and still questioning whether it was good or not during the first few minutes, but after a while I got really into it. Definitely should play 10/10. I will be getting the prequel Ensign as well

reviews.title: Honest Review
reviews.text: i don't normally review games. this one however, absolutely deserves one. i've been playing this game since high school, and i've always came back to it. one of my favorite games on the app store. it's quite a beautiful game that i highly recommend playing. i don't want to say too much about it, the mystery your first time playing it makes it that much more enjoyable. check it out, and don't give up.

reviews.title: Web vs App
reviews.text:
Wished i had played app version first. Story is better. Web version interface was preferred. So playing app felt odd.

That said, this is one of my top 5 gaming experiences EVER! Love this! Do not underestimate this game, with free web version, you expect less and thus have patience. With paying for app, expectations go up against other apps with graphics and A.D.D. pacing. This is old school at its best. mud, nethack, rogue. But better cus its got its own twist.

Not very replay-able, but a worthwhile one time experience

reviews.title: A great adventure!
reviews.text: For some this game won’t be entertaining, as it requires imagination and some may get bored with the words. I for one have loved playing this game, trying new ways to win each time. I’ve completed it countless time but each new game I play is better than the last. I suggest everyone give this game a chance, as it’s only 1.99$. If you want a game where you create basically your own path but still follow an interesting storyline this game is for you.

reviews.title: Still my favorite game❤️
reviews.text: I downloaded this app back when it was first launched and no matter how many apps I've downloaded since, this has always been my favorite. I still play this every once in a while and I get quicker every time. I'm so happy to be a part of this experience because I truly think this app is art. I won't go into details because you need to experience this for yourself, but I whole heartedly recommend this amazing app!

reviews.title: Slow but amazing
reviews.text: I first played this with a friend on his phone awhile ago, and thought it was slow, boring and monotonous. After playing it through myself, I fell in love with this game. I’ve gotten it on every device I own and have played it through. I have yet to beat the challenge mode! But, I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a beautiful and intriguing story. The controls are simple and easy but the story definitely makes up for it.

reviews.title: Terrible Awful Game!!!!!
reviews.text: First of all it’s just a word game. No graphics at all. Just words... Second, the game is just way too simple. For example you can’t trade anything. I have like 2000 wood and zero food. Why can’t I trade wood for food? I have 36 villagers and they eat the food and use the fur as quickly as I can get it. Why can’t I kick out some villagers? And finally, there are no instructions or directions. What can I use scales for? How do I get more fur?  There are so many problems with this game. Even if it was FREE they would be charging too much. And where are all of these five star ratings coming from? They are either bots or they are bots There’s no way those five star ratings are coming from human beings.

reviews.title: Phenomenal.
reviews.text: I’ve had this game on my phone for years. I never left a review until now for some reason. I think of this game every once in a while and how much it affected me. Listening to the audios from the creators afterwards was absolutely amazing. It was very interesting to hear about how difficult it was to create. While the game looks simple, it is by far one of the most complex games I’ve ever played. Don’t hesitate to play this game and support its amazing creators.

reviews.title: Good but a little overhyped
reviews.text: My daughter recommended this game as something that she was working on in her college level class. She was mesmerized by it so I went and got it. I have to agree that the story is compelling and the mechanics are very balanced. Still, mid-game it starts getting a bit too repetitive; and if you’re playing for the first time a bit directionless. That said, once I figured out what’s going on (kind of) it was quite nice to finish the story and see the replayability value.

reviews.title: Reviews, and mine
reviews.text:
Most the 1 star reviews are from people who don’t enjoy this style of game. I don’t recommend looking to far into them. Unless you want to see some elitism commentary and utter stupidity 

Spoilers ahead:

Now then, the games not for everyone and rating on scales is silly. Everyone has their own taste. But for $2 this game has a lot of replay value. It’s fun, the first play through you’ll buy huts, and regret it as your companion grows to despise you, yet you still love them. 

Next play through you’ll avoid the huts, keep it just the two of you. It’ll be slow and painful, you’ll appreciate whatever little they gather. Then, they’ll fall unconscious, you’ll be alone yet determined. You’ll make mistakes, fail and lose, but never give up. You’ll win and will feel accomplished.

reviews.title: A dark room review by a noob
reviews.text:
I found the game delightful, especially being fairly inexperienced with text based games. 
I never would have thought to use fists on my own and glad to have achieved this skill/perk on my second attempt after research on the game. During this second attempt I decided to show mercy and thought it really neat to get a sneaky perk. I enjoyed thinking about all the possible strategies.  Great game!

reviews.title: Wow what an incredible game
reviews.text: I loved it when I first started the game it took me a long time to figure out the dusty path. But once I got it it became really really awesome. It was really difficult at the sulfur mine. But I eventually pulled through and got to the end. That starship thing near the end wow I couldn’t have thought of anything better myself. The only thing I would suggest if you were to make another dark room would be to add dragons as some of the enemies

reviews.title: One of my favorites
reviews.text:
I had no idea what I was plunging myself into when I downloaded this game. I never did regret it either.
Being text based and eerily mysterious, A Dark Room has become one of the games I've spent most of my time on.

 I wholeheartedly encourage others to give ADR a try, they won't regret it.
In the meanwhile, with developers' notes, it's motivated me to be more creative with what I can do in hopes of creating something similar to this piece of art.

reviews.title: It’s so good
reviews.text: I don’t know if I’ve ever left a review on a game, but noting I’ve returned to this game every few years since high school and have now probably played it a good 4 or 5 times, I have to say this game is too notch. Very creative, incredibly atmospheric, and the minimalism is one of its many great strengths. Don’t want to say much more than that, as it is worth experiencing blind, but I truly love this game. 6 out of 5 stars if possible

reviews.title: A well made game
reviews.text: Really did not know what to expect - this is the first game I've gotten addicted to in a while. It's really mysterious and rewarding at the same time. There's no one right path - you can keep on exploring and experimenting and building. The game has lots of surprises that come at different times to keep things moving along. You get to be creative and each time you continue playing you'll encounter something new and different.

reviews.title: Great game well worth the $1
reviews.text: I had fun playing this game from start to finish. It took me 300+ hours and I enjoyed every second. It harkened back to old text games and requires a dose of imagination but it's very fun. I'd recommend it to anyone who is sick of social media and sick of the other junk on our phones. This is a perfect blend of the text and brightness capabilities and extremely creative. Oh that builder, I wish I could catch her. I'll try again without huts.

reviews.title: Wow.  Such an incredible game.
reviews.text: I rarely write reviews but this is just such a great game.  At first I was like “ok, it’s a fun little time waster”.  Then the depth just kept growing.  I threw it down several times after dying, only to be dragged back saying “ok, one more time”.  It’s a gripping game that keeps you thinking, but it’s not so difficult that you quit from frustration.  If you are losing, think more and try again.  Can’t recommend this title enough.  Woohoo 1000th review!  :D

reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.text: After finishing A Dark Room on the web for free I was more than willing to spend a little to get more out of it. I wasn’t disappointed! The new narrative and other bits that were different from the web version were exciting and getting to play it through more than once with new challenges meant the experience wouldn’t run out quickly by any means. Thank you to the developers!

reviews.title: A standard for text-based games
reviews.text: I thoroughly enjoyed my experience in A Dark Room, and for 2 bucks it’s absolutely worth your time and money. It’s great for short play sessions, maybe on a break or a longer session on a plane or train. The game can feel tense at times, especially when managing resources, so dont expect an idle game. My only issue is that A Dark Room constantly feels like it’s trying to get its message across, but it’s often too vague to do so.

reviews.title: Stress reliever
reviews.text: This game has been the to go to game whenever I’m in school. Whenever I am bored I know for sure that this game will get me excited. It really makes you feel accomplished fighting off beasts and figuring out the secrets within the game. There’s always a different to approach the life you live. It makes you feel like YOU are the character just trying to survive. I’ve played it like 9 times and I tell my friends all about it.

reviews.title: Beautiful and Haunting
reviews.text: I downloaded this game years ago and have since deleted and redownloaded it several times. This time I played it through to the end and was left with the same feeling I do when I finish my favorite book or movie. This game evokes such intense emotion in such a simplistic way. The thought and care that the creators put into the game is felt throughout. I will never forget this unique, mind-twisting experience.

reviews.title: Old design was way better
reviews.text: Love this game. Always come back to it. Don’t care for the new design though. The words on the buttons are mixed up. “the builder worried” should be “the worried builder” and it’s the same with the other button. “A tradepost merchants” instead of “a merchants tradepost.” Last update was 10 months ago, basically almost a year, so I’m hoping they fix this soon bc this game is too good to lose to some design flaws.

reviews.title: Several years of fun
reviews.text: I’ve been playing this game for several years, and every single play through is always a guessing game for me, I’m always surprised by what things I can find and learn about the game, every time I play through it again I get better and better and find new things I didn’t know existed, the replayability of this game is insurmountable.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text: Love to see other reviews of people saying there’s no plot or that the game is a sham. Love the simplicity, love the thought that went into it, and love the whole thing. Played through a few times now and every time the commentary is just great. Also great to see work is still being put in to this game years after I first played it. Thank you for this masterpiece.

reviews.title: Skeptical at first, but...
reviews.text:
This game is amazing! If you're a "graphics-are-king" tool, don't bother. If you want an enjoyable experience, pick this up and you won't regret it. 

Admittedly, I haven't reached the end of my journey with this one, but having played it for the last hour and a half, I wholeheartedly trust. The only reason that I stopped to write this review is because it is midnight, and if I don't take a break now, I won't sleep.

reviews.title: Haunting, Beautiful, and Simple
reviews.text: What a great game. I downloaded this on a whim after seeing it recommended on a Reddit thread about actually worthwhile mobile games, and I have to agree with the sentiment. This game marries simple resource management, world exploration, and storytelling in a minimalistic way, while still holding so much to offer the player in terms of lore, intrigue, and moral quandary. Definitely buy this game — it’s worth it.

reviews.title: Great game!
reviews.text:
Despite being all text based, this was one of the funnest games I've played since the last Fallout! I was amazed how it carried my imagination. Thanks so much

Update - a couple of years have passed, I’ve played the rest of your games and enjoyed them all. I still Google you regularly hoping for news about a new game - please make something else! A Dark Room remains the single best game I’ve ever played on my phone!

reviews.title: Groundbreaking still
reviews.text: After more than 10 years of occasional play throughs I have yet to find a more complete text based adventure on the App Store. The developers made every effort to make this game accessible to all people, even those with sensory disabilities. I will never forget this game for as long as I live. May the fire burn brightly for you, may it keep you warm.

reviews.title: Amazing game amazing story
reviews.text: I spent 228 mins on my first successful run through after about 3 resets (due to learning new mechanics and wanting to access them earlier) so I spent a total of four or five non stop days in hours to beat it(I’m slow) but the story and gameplay are phenomenal despite the simplicity and subtlety so full five stars on quality of gameplay and quantity of gameplay

reviews.title: Absolutely Stunning
reviews.text: The ambiguity and secretiveness of almost every action in this game is awe inspiring. This is not a game, this is an experience. I finished it in 281 minutes, about 4.5 hours the first time. Then 5.5 hours the second, and then about 7 hours the last time. This game gets better and better each time you play it. A true marvel in the world of gaming.

reviews.title: Wow. Just wow.
reviews.text: This game was so much fun. The lure to get more supplies, build more, explore more—it all fed that dopamine side of me without the game coming off a tacky. And the mystery of the game that slowly unfolded...just wow. I didn’t want to stop playing, because I needed to know, and...wow. Overall, a well crafted game that kept me engaged. Now that I beat it, well...I very well might try beating it again. Although I’m sure that she’d be disappointed...

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: I finished the game for the first time last night (304 minutes) and it was one of the best experiences I’ve ever had. I started off slow but it didn’t take long for me to be hooked. Don’t let the single screenshot fool you, this game is everything but simple. A special thank you to Amir and Micheal for creating this gem. I am now going on to replay the game with no huts and I’m very excited. Thank you very much.

reviews.title: Unique Genre of Gaming
reviews.text: This game is phenomenal. I have had the game for the past several years, just now beating the game for the first time. It is so unique in that it retains your interest whenever you come back to it. A lot of games have a tendency to get stale and you never become reintegrated. But, this game always has something new and inquisitive to offer. I would describe this game as a story-telling adventure and strategy.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: When starting this game, I didn't really get it or understand the point. But I pressed on anyways and was glad I did. A text based game sounded weird but it was actually awesome. So, for those of you wondering if you should buy this... You should, you'll be glad you did. Don't give up early on. The seemingly uneventful beginning is more eventful than you will realize. Thanks for a great game experience.

reviews.title: Unforgettable
reviews.text: Never would I have thought that a game using only text could illicit such emotion. The wanderer’s relationship with the builder is one of tragedy, or of love and sacrifice, depending on how we choose to play. The simplistic layout betrays its deeply complex gameplay loop. In an age of AAA $75 games, this game will always endure as a must have experience. 10/10, would, and have, played again!

reviews.title: I hate the new UI
reviews.text: I I used to play this game quite a while ago, and I really liked it. Perfect tension and world building/story telling. I wanted to replay it today, and when i opened it up I was so confused. The new UI is so unintuitive and abrasive. It completely messed up the creepy tense vibe the game used to have :( Now it just gives me a headache. It’s so much harder to read what’s on the screen and to quickly scan for info. What was the point of changing something that was perfectly fine before? I’m so disappointed

reviews.title: Such A Unique Experience
reviews.text: This was such a fun game. I stumbled upon it while searching out a similar game from my childhood (that I absolutely could not remember the name of; only that it was on a Windows 98 game disc) I’m actually kind of sad that I got through it so quickly, but definitely would play it again to see if I got a different experience. Thank you!

reviews.title: soulful, gripping and memorable
reviews.text:
A Dark Room is truly special, it could be a thesis representing the concept of “less is more.” 

I feel as though “game” might be an inadequate term to describe A Dark Room, I find “experience” to be more apt.

So much is left up to the imagination while at the same time providing a poignantly bleak and uniquely captivating context for your imagination to blossom within.

Overall, this is the best simple mobile experience ever created; no unreal engine, fancy graphics, or obvious narrative necessary.

A Dark Room is a masterpiece as many before have witnessed, so if you haven’t played it yet, I envy you and the profound journey you will have within your mind sitting with this experience.

reviews.title: A masterpiece
reviews.text: Truly one of the best games I’ve ever played. Hard stop. I have played on every platform and console, old and new. This game makes you feel a connection to not only the player character, but the builder and the world. This game truly represents the term less is more. Don’t forget to listen to the audio journals of the devs when you beat the game!

reviews.title: Astounding!
reviews.text: I absolutely love this game. I first played a few years back but the story line brought me back it almost felt like my first time again. I finished the game and on my second play through the game starts to crash when I play and listen to the secrets this didn’t start to happen until I ventured down the dusty path “walking the path” started to play. Still worth it!!

reviews.title: Supercalifragilisticexpialodoschus!!!!!
reviews.text:
Even though the sound of it is simply quite atrocious. I feel that this game is Supercalifragilisticexpialodoschus!!!!! I know that it has been four years since the game was number one, I feel that it deserves it still from me. This was the first game that I was able to play since went blind, so, thank you amir...

P.S. I wish I could give a ten star review.

reviews.title: In Love with it even now
reviews.text: Although this game has been out for a while and everyone has seen much of it I still feel the need to say how amazing this game. It’s intriguing and interesting to say the least, the simple start  and the game all together has so much more meaning that is overseen at first, but now after beating it I’m still going back to play it again years later.

reviews.title: Wild and unexpected!
reviews.text: I very seldom leave reviews. This game blew me away. Wasn’t sure what to expect. It started out with a simple enough idea. It was amazing to watch it grow more complicated and with each phase draw me deeper in. To the point that I could not put it down. This is much more than a game it is a thought provoking work of art that is to my own surprise the greatest mobile game I have ever played. Well done!

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text:
In the spirit of the game’s design, I am just going to keep this simple: What a beautiful, intriguing experience.
I picked this back up after not finishing it several years ago and hardly put it back down until I had finally reached the end.

The experience kind of stays with you for a bit afterwards. I really appreciate works that can accomplish that; it’s no small feat. Kudos to Michael and Amir.

reviews.title: An amazing game
reviews.text: I played this game in 2016 while I was in highschool in the computer room. I loved it then but I never completed it until now. I saw it was on the App Store and I was ecstatic!!! It’s such a great adventure and I loved the way it was designed and set before you. It leaves a lot to your imagination and I had such a fun time playing. I dearly hope to see more!

reviews.title: Definitely a must try
reviews.text: This game is extremely polished for what it is. It took me around 2-3 hours on my 3rd play through. The first time playing a dark room was the quintessential video game experience, learning the quirks of the game and finding a way to progress. The underlying story is ambiguous and gloomy but the game does not run off of the narrative. In 2023 it still holds up and is definitely worth a play through.

reviews.title: Awesome game
reviews.text: For a game without graphics I wasn’t expecting much. With that being said this is actually one of the funnest games I have played on my phone. It’s easy to pick up and kinda hard to put down sometimes, it hooks you with the traveling and trying to beat it but not knowing what’s around the corner. The Ensign is just as fun if not more because it’s all adventure.

reviews.title: Best iOS game I’ve ever played
reviews.text: This is probably one of the best iOS games I’ve played the constant progression keeps me locked in, just waiting and wondering to see what you can find outside of the village. Something you have to experience for yourself even tho it’s not completely visual I could play this game for hours, the simplicity gives it extreme replay ability.

reviews.title: A very pleasant surprise
reviews.text: I had seen this game on the top 25 and had wondered why it was so popular, the game seemed very basic. Eventually I decided to give the game a try and right from the start I loved it; the story developed far more than expected and had a very deep meaning. If you are thinking of getting this game, you definitely should.

reviews.title: Oh man what a game
reviews.text: I actually played it for a while a few years back and uninstalled Coz I didn’t have the patience to figure it out. But this time round, man oh man, what a concept. Superbly done. Keeps you playing Coz you just want to get the next cool ‘supply’ and building! Haven’t even finished a quarter of the map. Can’t get enough of this! Hats off….

reviews.title: A great game
reviews.text: To be honest I love a dark room because not only is it a game that is fun if you play it again but also because it’s a challenging game, I would suggest it to anyone who is looking for a great game with a lot of story and is looking for a challenge. So I hope that you found review helpful and if you did than that’s good and I hope hat you enjoy the rest of your day/night!

reviews.title: Unique and Incredible
reviews.text:
I enjoy clickers with a point, an arc: Space Plan, Universal Paper Clips, even cookie clicker’s emergent narrative. This one easily plays at that level.

I’ll be honest: I bought it, clicked for about 2 minutes and then closed it and forgot about it. Luckily, with an empty weekend and a reminder about the game from Reddit I have it a second shot. Can’t say how happy I am that I did.

reviews.title: Well spent weekend
